headline: Doubling the chain to six levels costs `next-yak` nothing and `@yak/solid` almost nothing either — its penalty was already paid at the first `styled(Component)`.

microbench.why: `next-yak` leads at 1.50M renders/s, faster than it manages at depth 3, because the whole chain still collapses into one wrapper no matter how long it is. `vanilla` drops to 964,000 running six functions. `yak-solid` at 236,000 is within 2% of its depth-3 number: once the first `styled(Component)` has forced a Solid component per element, the five levels above it are merged at construction and cost almost nothing more. `tailwind-merge` at 422,000 is the lane depth hurts most, re-resolving the conflicting utilities at every level.

autocannon.why: `next-yak` holds 1,140 req/s while `vanilla` falls to 817 — the flattened chain is what keeps the per-request cost constant across depth. `panda` at 142 req/s and `yak-solid` at 194 are the two lanes whose per-instance work grows with the tree.

attribution.why: `next-yak` renders in 0.796 ms with 0.372 ms of lib self-time, unchanged from depth 3. `cn` at 1.22 ms and `vanilla` at 1.24 ms follow, and the contrast with `tailwind-merge` at 2.70 ms — 1.94 ms of it in its own runtime — is the case's clearest reading of what a per-level merge costs when nothing caches it. `vanilla-solid` books 2.58 ms of component self-time for its six functions, and `yak-solid`'s 6.30 ms is again mostly framework.

hydrate.why: `vanilla-solid` at 39.4 ms leads, and the React lanes cluster near 50 ms. `yak-solid` at 71.4 ms carries the same unfolded wrapper into hydration. `emotion` at 116 ms and `goober` at 111 ms sit high in every compose case.

inp.why: `yak-solid` at 3.6 ms and `vanilla-solid` at 3.8 ms lead a field where the React lanes answer near 7.9 ms — with the caveat that React writes nothing to the DOM on this pass and the Solid lanes do. `goober` at 22.8 ms and `panda` at 16.2 ms re-run their runtimes for all six levels.

mount.why: `vanilla-solid` mounts in 27.2 ms, `yak-solid` in 52.0 ms, and the React field spans 73.5 ms to 113 ms. Depth costs the Solid lanes visibly and the React lanes almost nothing, because layout, not composition, sets the React mount time.

renderTiming.why: One style recalculation per lane. Six levels of declarations resolve to one class list on one element, so the style engine sees exactly what it sees at depth 1.

payload.why: `vanilla` is the floor at 3,075 gz B and the compile-time lanes stay within 1.2 kB of it: six levels of declarations gzip into roughly what one level produces. `yak-solid` at 9,243 B carries Solid's runtime and its hydration-keyed markup. `cn` at 16,502 B and `styled-components` at 16,787 B ship their runtimes regardless of depth.

nsweep.why: `next-yak` holds 2.82 ms at 4,000 instances against 4.44 ms for `vanilla` and 11.6 ms for `vanilla-solid`, so the flattened chain is the only structure in the case with no per-level slope. `panda` at 19.1 ms and `yak-solid` at 18.9 ms bend hardest.

crossCase: The upper bracket of the sweep that starts at the Examples `compose-1` and `compose-3`. `vanilla` degrades with depth as expected, 1.89M to 1.28M to 964,000 renders/s, since it runs one more function per level. `next-yak` runs 2.11M, 1.39M and 1.50M — flat after the first wrapper. `yak-solid` runs 5.08M, 241,000 and 236,000: the cliff is the first unfolded level, and levels four through six add 2%.
